source.title: An Exploratory Replica-Overlap Probe of the Grokking Transition

record.tranche_reason: The study trains small networks on modular addition and reports memorization and held-out generalization outcomes relevant to V1, but its main replica-overlap probe is a different measure from the original grokking measurements.
record.gate_note: Rows record the study's grokking incidence and transition-epoch results, plus its transition-related replica-overlap measurements not covered by the listed versions. The overlap instrument is explicitly reported as invalid because its permutations do not preserve the network function. The ensemble-size result is omitted because it does not measure a listed claim version or directly report grokking behavior.
record.test_reason: Same task family and measure as Power et al.: modular addition at p=113, tracking held-out accuracy over training across train fractions, with 16 seeded replicas each. The grokking-reliability results (Table 1, Figs 1–2) bear directly on V1. The replica-overlap probe, the study's main aim, measures a different construct and is declared invalid by the authors.
record.authors_conclusion: Essentially correct. The registered RSB overlap test is UNDETERMINED: the alignment is invalid, the precision rail failed, and there were protocol deviations. The post-hoc dip interval is uninformative because the test has zero power. The overlap sd rose about 5.6×, which the authors call detectable widening, but they do not treat it as validated. Grokking rates of 0/16, 11/16 and 16/16 are descriptive only because fraction is confounded with split.
record.recipe_differences: Uses modular addition with p = 113 and a small-network grokking setup, with 16 independently seeded replicas per configuration. It adds a replica-overlap probe and uses a stopping rule based on test accuracy ≥ 99% for 1,000 consecutive epochs or a 40,000-epoch ceiling. Each train fraction has a different split seed.
record.method_sensitivity: Observed grokking rates and transition epochs differ across the three realized train-fraction-by-split configurations; because each fraction uses a different split seed, the study cannot attribute the differences to fraction.

fits_no_version.finding: Across the frac40 transition, replica prediction agreement goes from 0.023 to 1.0, which is forced by accuracy. The aligned weight-overlap sd rises about 5.6×, but the alignment is non-function-preserving and the dip test is powerless.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Independently seeded replicas' aligned weight-overlap distribution widens across grokking. This is unvalidated because the alignment is invalid.

record.problems: The alignment permutes weights without corresponding biases and does not handle head-internal symmetries, so it does not preserve the network function. The registered fp32/fp64 precision rail failed; the dip test had zero power at the simulated separations in a post-hoc calibration. No pre-analysis power calibration or equivalence margin was specified. Several registered controls did not run, including matched-epoch overlap controls. Only frac40 cleared the checkpoint-completeness gate for overlap analysis. There was one split seed per train fraction, confounding fraction with split identity.
record.rows_left_out: O2 ensemble-size and loss results in Section 5.3 and Figure 4 were left out because they do not test any listed version or directly report grokking behavior.

untested.parts: Epoch at which training accuracy saturates is not reported, so the lag is only implied. The dependence of delay on train fraction is shown only descriptively across three fraction×split configurations that are fully confounded (one split seed each). Results cover a single task (p=113 addition) and a single architecture.
No circuit, Fourier or progress-measure analysis.
No non-algorithmic data and no initialization or weight-norm manipulation.
Weight decay is not varied; no critical-size or ungrokking test.
Algorithms of replicas are not identified. Weight overlap uses a non-function-preserving alignment, and function agreement is forced by accuracy.
Optimizer and numerical choices are not varied. The fp32/fp64 rail concerns the overlap computation, not training.

missing.what: Memorization reached by 16/16 replicas in every configuration, including nogrok. This establishes the memorize-then-generalize sequence; there is no row for it.
Final-epoch distributions per configuration (frac40 4,372–26,838, mean 11,525; frac30 31,063–39,999, mean 37,001).

record.verdict_notes: The study is not one of V1's original sources. V1 evidence is a side result of the sweep. No row's subject, value or baseline is wrong. The r5 mean transition epoch (9,899) differs from the mean final epoch (11,525) because they measure different things. No instructions were found in the text.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not quantify the exact time at which training accuracy saturates relative to the test transition. Train fraction is confounded with split identity, so it does not isolate a training-set-size effect. frac25 was observed only through the 40,000-epoch ceiling.
The study does not measure formation of a generalizing circuit, removal of memorizing components, or continuous mechanistic progress measures.
No non-algorithmic data, initialization-scale sweep, or weight-norm manipulation is tested.
No LLM pretraining or realistic-data fine-tuning is studied.
The study does not test weight decay or another low-norm bias as an explanation, a critical dataset size, or ungrokking.
The study does not identify or compare the algorithms learned by independent runs.
The study notes a numerical-precision rail failure but does not test whether optimizer or numerical artifacts produce the grokking delay or whether controlling them removes it.

rows.subject: frac25 (16 independently seeded replicas; aggregate)
rows.stage_stated: Trained to the stopping criterion or 40,000-epoch ceiling
rows.operation_detail: Train on modular addition and count replicas reaching post-grokking
rows.note: All 16 replicas memorized, but none reached a post-grokking checkpoint within budget. The authors say this is a reachability result, not evidence against RSB.
rows.check: State is right for 'jump within 40,000 epochs', but this is censored at the budget. The authors call it a reachability result, so it cannot distinguish no grokking from a longer delay.

rows.subject: frac30 (11 grokked replicas; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Record first epoch at which test accuracy is at least 50%
rows.note: The authors describe the span as about 9,000 epochs; the latest transition still leaves 2,161 epochs in the budget.
rows.check: The row measures transition epochs of the 11 replicas that did grok, and they show a long delay (mean 33,765). The five non-grokkers belong to r2, so 'partial' double-counts them. Caveat: the transition is the first epoch with test accuracy ≥50%, and the training-saturation epoch is not reported.

rows.operation_detail: Report mean transition epoch, where transition is first test accuracy of at least 50%
rows.note: The 16 replicas stopped early after meeting the sustained test-accuracy criterion; their final epochs were 4,372–26,838.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, Table 1: frac40 mean transition epoch 9,899, defined as first test accuracy ≥50%; Section 3 gives final epochs 4,372–26,838.

rows.subject: frac25 (16 replicas; aggregate)
rows.value: Sample means and medians lie near the chance floor; median 0.87%. Two replicas attain 4.6% and 5.8%.
rows.note: The authors report the two outliers descriptively (n = 2), not as evidence of partial generalization.

source_check.locator_found: Section 5.1, Figure 2 and accompanying text: chance floor 1/113 ≈0.885%; frac25 median 0.87%, with two outliers at 4.6% and 5.8%.

rows.subject: nogrok (16 independently seeded replicas; aggregate)
rows.operation_detail: Measure held-out test accuracy on the random-label control

conditions.value: i.i.d. random labels shared across replicas

rows.note: The control did not generalize. Its registered matched-epoch overlap role was not performed.
rows.check: Random-label control with no generalizable structure. It cannot show or fail to show grokking, so it does not bear on V1 itself. It only validates the chance floor.

rows.subject: frac40 replicas (aggregate pairwise comparison)
rows.operation_detail: Measure agreement of unpermuted replicas' top-1 predictions on the shared held-out set
rows.note: This measures agreement between replicas, not the listed claim versions' mechanism or test-accuracy trajectory.
rows.check: Post-grokking qfn=1.0 is mechanically forced by every replica reaching 100% test accuracy, as the authors state. It is not evidence of shared algorithm (V6).

rows.subject: frac40 replicas (aggregate pairwise comparison)
rows.operation_detail: Measure standard deviation of aligned pairwise weight-space overlap qwt

conditions.value: weight permutations applied without corresponding biases

rows.note: The paper says the non-function-preserving alignment makes every overlap value inherit the defect; the authors describe widening but do not treat it as a validated RSB result.

rows.subject: frac40 replicas (aggregate pairwise comparison)
rows.operation_detail: Compare Hartigan dip statistic for aligned qwt distributions
rows.note: The interval contains zero, but post-hoc calibration assigns the dip test zero power at the simulated separations; the authors call the interval uninformative, not evidence of no change.

relationships.condition: frac40 (all 16 replicas) and the 11 grokked frac30 replicas, modular addition p=113
relationships.reason: All replicas memorized, then test accuracy reached ≥99% sustained. The transition was later at the smaller fraction (mean 33,765 vs 9,899 epochs), an ordering consistent with V1 but confounded with split seed (r2, r3, r4, r5).
relationships.display_finding: All 16 replicas at 40% and the 11 successful replicas at 30% memorized before sustaining at least 99% test accuracy, with mean transitions at 9,899 and 33,765 epochs respectively, although training fraction was confounded with split seed.

source_check.label: supports
source_check.condition: frac40 (all 16 replicas) and the 11 grokked frac30 replicas, modular addition p=113
source_check.reason: r2–r5 document memorization followed by sustained near-perfect test accuracy in these replicas. Mean transition epochs are 33,765 for frac30 and 9,899 for frac40; this ordering is descriptive because fraction and split identity change together.

relationships.condition: frac25 (0/16) and the 5 non-grokking frac30 replicas, within a 40,000-epoch budget
relationships.reason: Replicas memorized but test accuracy stayed near chance (median 0.87%) within budget. Grokking is seed-dependent and absent at the lowest fraction in this budget, though this may reflect longer delay (r1, r2, r6).
relationships.display_finding: All 16 replicas at 25% and five replicas at 30% memorized but remained near chance within 40,000 epochs, with median test accuracy of 0.87%.

source_check.label: limits_scope
source_check.condition: frac25 (0/16) and the 5 non-grokking frac30 replicas, within a 40,000-epoch budget
source_check.reason: r1, r2 and r6 establish incomplete grokking reliability within the observation budget. The 0.87% median applies specifically to frac25; no corresponding median is reported for the five unsuccessful frac30 replicas. Longer delays remain possible.

relation.reason: Its own training results directly bear on V1, independently of the invalid replica-overlap instrument.

tranche.reason: The study uses the original modular-addition task family and directly measures held-out accuracy, delayed transitions and grokking success across training fractions. Its additional overlap probe does not replace these direct measurements.

source_check.notes: Transition epochs measure the first ≥50% test-accuracy crossing, not the post-memorization gap. The primary RSB test is UNDETERMINED because its instrument is invalid; this does not invalidate the separately reported grokking counts.
